title: Proof
body_md:
The inequality $\theta \geq \mu$ is a direct consequence of Assumption \ref{ass_1}. To establish $w=\theta e$, note that 
\begin{align*}
\theta(x,t)e(x,t) &= e(x,t) \intop_0^1 \Psi'\left(\hat{z}(x,t)+\tau e(x,t)\right)d\tau \\
&= \left[\Psi\left(\hat{z}(x,t)+\tau e(x,t)\right)\right]_{\tau=0}^{\tau=1} \\
&= \Psi(z(x,t)) - \Psi(\hat{z}(x,t)) \\
&= w(x,t).
\end{align*}
Finally, $\mathop{\mathrm{sign}}\nolimits(w) = \mathop{\mathrm{sign}}\nolimits(e)$ follows from $w=\theta e$ and $\theta \geq \mu >0$.

label: eq_riccati
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\xi$ be the unique solution in $(0,\pi/2)$ to $\xi \tan(\xi) = k$, and $\rho \in \mathscr{C}^1((0,1];\mathbb{R}_{>0})$ be given by
$$\rho(x):=\xi \cot(\xi x).$$
Using $\frac{d}{dx}\cot(\xi x) = -\xi\left(1+\cot^2(\xi x)\right)$, we have
\begin{align}\label{eq_riccati}
\rho'(x)+\rho(x)^2 = -\lambda \quad \forall x\in (0,1),
\end{align}
and
\begin{align}\label{eq_rho1}
\rho(1) = \xi \cot(\xi) = \frac{\xi^2}{\xi \tan \xi} = \frac{\lambda}{k} .
\end{align}
Next, let $\delta \in (0,1)$ and note that
\begin{align*}
0 \leq&~ \intop_\delta^1 \left(\phi'(x) - \rho (x)\phi(x)\right)^2dx \\
=&~ \intop_\delta^1 \phi'(x)^2 dx - \intop_\delta^1 \rho(x)\left(\phi(x)^2\right)'dx + \intop_\delta^1 \rho(x)^2\phi(x)^2dx \\
=&~ \intop_\delta^1 \phi'(x)^2dx - \rho(1)\phi(1)^2 + \rho(\delta)\phi(\delta)^2 + \intop_\delta^1 \left(\rho'(x)+\rho(x)^2\right)\phi(x)^2 dx .
\end{align*}
Substituting \eqref{eq_riccati} and \eqref{eq_rho1} and rearranging,
\begin{align}\label{eq_delta}
\intop_\delta^1 \phi'(x)^2dx \geq \frac{\lambda}{k}\phi(1)^2 + \lambda\intop_\delta^1\phi(x)^2dx
- \rho(\delta)\phi(\delta)^2 .
\end{align}
Since $\phi\in \mathscr{C}^1([0,1])$ and $\phi(0)=0$, we have
$$|\phi(\delta)| \leq \delta \max_{x\in [0,1]}|\phi'(x)|.$$
Moreover, $\cot(s) \leq 1/s$ for all
$s\in(0,\pi/2)$, so that 
$$\rho(\delta)\leq \frac{1}{\delta}.$$
Hence
$$\rho(\delta)\phi(\delta)^2 \leq \delta \left(\max_{x\in [0,1]}|\phi'(x)|\right)^2 \to 0 \ \ \text{as $\delta \to 0^+$}.$$
Letting $\delta \to 0^+$ in \eqref{eq_delta} and dividing by $\lambda$
yields \eqref{eq_poincare}.
